title: 5 days in Japan: Tokyo, Kyoto

brief.request: Plan a 5-day trip to Japan. Tokyo + Kyoto. $3,000 budget. Love food and temples, hate crowds.

slots.name: Senso-ji
slots.why: Tokyo's most iconic temple, matches temples like
slots.crowd_tactic: Peak site, included because must-do. Arrive 06:30, before shops and tour groups open

slots.name: Asakusa food alleys (Nakamise Shopping Street, Kappabashi Hondori)
slots.why: Ningyo-yaki, senbei, age-manju on Nakamise, kitchenware and sample-food shops on Kappabashi
slots.crowd_tactic: Walk Nakamise at opening, before 09:00, then shift to Kappabashi (mostly a wholesale street, never crowded), rather than fighting the midday Nakamise crush

slots.name: Asakusa izakaya row (Hoppy Street / Okamoto Hoppy Street)
slots.why: Grilled offal (motsuyaki), Hoppy malt drink, simple izakaya plates
slots.crowd_tactic: Go right at the 16:00 opening on a weekday, seats at the outdoor tables fill fast after 18:00

slots.name: Nezu Shrine
slots.why: Quiet shrine with a torii tunnel, alternative to Fushimi-style photo spots in Tokyo

slots.name: Yanaka Ginza
slots.why: Menchi-katsu croquettes, senbei, skewered dango, neighbourhood snacks
slots.crowd_tactic: Weekday mid-afternoon, well before the sunset photo crowd gathers at the Yuyake Dandan steps

slots.name: Ueno food street (Ameyoko Market)
slots.why: Street seafood, cheap sushi, fresh fruit, fried snacks
slots.crowd_tactic: Weekday late morning avoids the weekend shoulder-to-shoulder crowds along the main arcade

slots.name: Tokyo to Kyoto, Nozomi Shinkansen (reserved)
slots.why: Only inter-city move of the trip

slots.name: Honenin Temple
slots.why: Quiet moss-and-thatched-gate temple, low visitor count
slots.crowd_tactic: Instead of the crowded Philosopher's Path temples, come here

slots.name: Pontocho Alley (Kaisentonya, Fumiya Nishiki area)
slots.crowd_tactic: Go on a weekday, riverside seats fill fast on weekends

slots.name: Kiyomizu-dera
slots.why: Landmark wooden temple overlooking the city
slots.crowd_tactic: Peak site, included because must-do. Arrive 07:00 at opening

slots.name: Teramachi-Kawaramachi food street (GYUKATSU Katsugyu, Kyoto Tempura Ten no Meshi)
slots.crowd_tactic: Eat before 11:30 or after 14:00 to skip the lunch line

slots.name: Kyoto Station dining and depachika (Kyoto Porta, JR Kyoto Isetan B2 food hall, Kyoto Tower Sando food hall)
slots.why: Isetan depachika bento and wagashi, Katsukura tonkatsu, Kyoto Tower Sando food-court ramen
slots.crowd_tactic: Eat before the 12:00 commuter lunch rush or after 19:30 when depachika counters start marking down bento, rather than queueing at peak Isetan B2 hours

slots.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
slots.crowd_tactic: Peak site, included because must-do. Arrive 06:00, before tour buses

slots.name: Departure from Kyoto
slots.why: No return leg or flight time in the brief, so left open

stays.why: Senso-ji on foot, izakaya and street-food alleys, well connected by rail
Old-town shrines, low foot traffic, away from Shibuya and Shinjuku crowds
Walking distance to Kiyomizu-dera and the temple lanes, best done at opening

examples.name: Mitsui Garden Hotel Kyoto Sanjo Premier

stays.why: Station access for Fushimi Inari and departure, station-front dining

intercity.mode: Nozomi Shinkansen, reserved seat, Tokaido Shinkansen

lines.basis: 4 nights x midpoint 115 of $80 to $150 band (estimate)
train 120 (midpoint of $100 to $140 band, estimate; seeded reserved fare is 88.48) + 5 days x midpoint 11.50 of $8 to $15 local transit band (estimate)
5 days x midpoint 42.50 of $30 to $55 band (estimate)
5 temple entries scheduled x midpoint 6.50 of $3 to $10 band (estimate)

alternatives: Move Tokyo stay from a central ward to a quieter area like Asakusa or Nippori (already applied)
Swap one Shinkansen reserved seat for a non-reserved car on off-peak trains
Cut one sit-down dinner per two days in favour of street food or a convenience-store meal
Skip paid temple grounds beyond the main hall
Use a multi-day subway pass instead of single tickets in Kyoto

crowd_strategy: Three peak sites (Senso-ji, Kiyomizu-dera, Fushimi Inari) kept because they are must-do, each placed at a gate-opening slot (06:30, 07:00, 06:00) from a base within walking or station reach
The second temple in each city is a quiet one instead of a second peak site: Nezu Shrine in Tokyo, Honenin in Kyoto
Stay areas are Asakusa, Nezu/Yanaka, Higashiyama and Kyoto Station, chosen for low foot traffic or opening-time access, not Shibuya, Shinjuku or Gion
Every food slot carries a timing tactic from the destinations file
Skipped Meiji Jingu, Gotoku-ji, Zojo-ji, Gioji and Nishiki Market because they sit outside the day zones

checks.label: Fits in 5 days
checks.reason: Exactly 5 day headings, numbered Day 1 to Day 5, each with at least one scheduled slot (Day 5 has one morning slot, afternoon and evening marked free for departure).

checks.label: Includes Tokyo, Kyoto
checks.reason: Tokyo has Day 1 and Day 2 in full. Kyoto has Day 4 in full plus Day 3 (arrival afternoon and evening) and Day 5 (morning).

checks.label: Within $3000
checks.reason: Recomputed from the budget lines: stay 4 x 115 = 460.00, transport 120 + 5 x 11.50 = 177.50, food 5 x 42.50 = 212.50, activities 5 x 6.50 = 32.50, subtotal 882.50, buffer 10% = 88.25, total 970.75. Matches the stated total and is under the $3000 limit by 2029.25. All lines are estimates except the seeded rail fare of 88.48; international flights are excluded.

checks.label: Matches food, temples
checks.reason: Every day has at least one temple or food slot: Day 1 Senso-ji plus two food slots, Day 2 Nezu Shrine plus two food slots, Day 3 Honenin plus Pontocho food, Day 4 Kiyomizu-dera plus two food slots, Day 5 Fushimi Inari Taisha. The Kind column uses must-do and nice-to-have rather than temple and food, so the mapping was read from the What and Why it fits columns.

checks.label: Avoids crowds
checks.reason: Day 2 evening slot (Ameyoko Market) carries the tactic 'Weekday late morning avoids the weekend shoulder-to-shoulder crowds', which cannot be applied to an evening slot, so that slot has no usable crowd tactic. All other venue slots have a concrete tactic (gate-opening times 06:30, 07:00, 06:00, before 09:00, 16:00 weekday opening, before 11:30 or after 14:00, before 12:00 or after 19:30). Warning only: Day 3 Honenin's tactic is a site choice ('instead of the crowded Philosopher's Path temples') rather than a timing tactic.

checks.label: Travel time realistic
checks.reason: Inter-city day (Day 3) allots 195 min, which is the 135 min seeded Nozomi ride plus 60 min buffer. Stated intra-city transit per day: Day 1 0 min, Day 2 66 min (52 + 14), Day 3 89 min, Day 4 38 min, Day 5 40 min, all within 90. Warning: Day 2 Yanaka Ginza to Ameyoko and Day 3 Honenin to Pontocho are 'could not verify', so the true Day 2 and Day 3 totals may exceed 90 (Nezu Shrine to Ameyoko alone is 26 min walk per the tool, which would put Day 2 at 92 if that leg is similar).

failures.instruction: Day 2 evening Ameyoko Market slot has a late-morning tactic that does not fit an evening visit, so either give that slot an evening-specific concrete tactic from the destinations file or move the slot to the time the tactic covers.
